[[File:Edison Liu 2022.png|alt=Portrait of Edison T. Liu, M.D. 2022|thumb]]
'''Edison Tak-Bun Liu''' is an American chemist and former president and CEO of [[The Jackson Laboratory]] and director of its [[NCI-designated Cancer Center]] (2012–2021). He previously served as founding executive director of the [[Genome Institute of Singapore|Genome Institute of Singapore (GIS)]], chairman of the [[Health Sciences Authority]], and president of the [[Human Genome Organization|Human Genome Organization (HUGO)]] (2007–2013).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hutchinson |first1=Ezzie |title=Edison Liu — Director of the Genome Institute of Singapore |url=https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanonc/article/PIIS1470-2045(00)00394-6/fulltext |website=[[The Lancet Oncology]] |pages=385–388 |language=English |doi=10.1016/S1470-2045(00)00394-6 |date=1 June 2001}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Edison T. Liu |url=https://themedicinemaker.com/power-list/2017/edison-t-liu |website=The Medicine Maker |language=en}}</ref>

From 1997 to 2001, he was scientific director of the [[National Cancer Institute]]'s Division of Clinical Sciences. At the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] (1987–1996), he held leadership roles at the [[Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center]], UNC School of Public Health, and [[CALGB]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Watch: Like a Boss Now: One-on-one with Dr. Edison Liu, President and CEO of The Jackson Laboratory |url=https://www.pressherald.com/2020/05/04/like-a-boss-now-one-on-one-with-dr-edison-liu-president-of-the-jackson-laboratory/ |website=[[Press Herald]] |date=4 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Kevin |first1=Brian |title=Dr. Edison Liu's Favorite Place |url=https://downeast.com/my-favorite-place/dr-edison-lius-favorite-place/ |website=[[Down East Magazine]] |date=18 April 2019}}</ref>

==Education==
Edison T. Liu earned his B.S. in Chemistry and Psychology from [[Stanford University]] in 1973, followed by an M.D. from the [[Stanford University School of Medicine]] in 1978. He completed his internship (1978–1979) and residency (1979–1980) at Barnes Hospital, affiliated with [[Washington University in St. Louis]]. Liu then pursued an oncology fellowship at [[Stanford University]] (1980–1982) and a hematology fellowship at [[University of California, San Francisco|University of California San Francisco]], Moffitt Hospital (1982–1985).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Stevens |first1=Shelby |title=The Future of Genomics and Breast Cancer According to Dr. Edison T. Liu |url=https://thecolgatemaroonnews.com/2405/news/the-future-of-genomics-and-breast-cancer-according-to-dr-edison-t-liu/ |website=[[The Colgate Maroon-News]]}}</ref> From 1983 to 1987, he was a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Microbiology at the [[University of California, San Francisco|University of California at San Francisco]], working in the laboratory of Dr. [[J. Michael Bishop]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Jackson Laboratory’s Edison Liu Is Keynote at 40th Annual Meeting of the Academy |url=https://ctcase.org/jackson-laboratorys-edison-liu-is-keynote-at-40th-annual-meeting-of-the-academy/ |website=[[Connecticut Academy of Science and Engineering]] |date=11 May 2015}}</ref>

==Professional appointments==
Liu has served as Professor, President Emeritus, and Honorary Fellow at [[The Jackson Laboratory]], where he was previously President and CEO from 2011 to 2021. From 2001 to 2011, he was Executive Director of the [[Genome Institute of Singapore]], and concurrently served as Chairman of the Governing Board of the [[Health Sciences Authority]] of Singapore (2007–2011). Prior to that, Liu was Director of the Division of Clinical Sciences at the [[National Cancer Institute]] (1996–2001).<ref>{{cite web |title=Dr. Edison Liu |url=https://www.themainemag.com/2379-dr-edison-liu/ |website=The Maine Mag |date=14 January 2014}}</ref>

At the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], he held several academic and leadership roles, including Chief of the Division of Medical Genetics and Professor in the Departments of Medicine, Epidemiology, Biochemistry, and Biophysics (1995–1996), Associate Professor (1993–1995), and Assistant Professor in Medicine and Oncology (1987–1993). He also directed the NIH-designated Specialized Program of Research Excellence in Breast Cancer from 1992 to 1996.<ref>{{cite web |title=Edison T. Liu of The Jackson Laboratory named 2016 AAAS Fellow |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/741223 |website=[[EurekAlert!]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Research==
Liu's scientific research has focused on the [[functional genomics]] of human cancers, particularly [[breast cancer]] (identifying the tandem duplicator phenotype genomic configuration<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Menghi|first1=Francesca|last2=Barthel|first2=Floris P.|last3=Yadav|first3=Vinod|last4=Tang|first4=Ming|last5=Ji|first5=Bo|last6=Tang|first6=Zhonghui|last7=Carter|first7=Gregory W.|last8=Ruan|first8=Yijun|last9=Scully|first9=Ralph|last10=Verhaak|first10=Roel G.W.|last11=Jonkers|first11=Jos|last12=Liu|first12=Edison|date=2018|title=The Tandem Duplicator Phenotype Is a Prevalent Genome-Wide Cancer Configuration Driven by Distinct Gene Mutations|journal=Cancer Cell|language=en|volume=34|issue=2|pages=197–210.e5|doi=10.1016/j.ccell.2018.06.008|pmc=6481635|pmid=30017478}}</ref>), discovering new oncogenes (AXL family of receptor tyrosine kinases<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=O'Bryan|first1=J. P.|last2=Frye|first2=R. A.|last3=Cogswell|first3=P. C.|last4=Neubauer|first4=A.|last5=Kitch|first5=B.|last6=Prokop|first6=C.|last7=R Espinosa|first7=3rd|last8=Beau|first8=M. M. Le|last9=Earp|first9=H. S.|last10=Liu|first10=E. T.|date=1991|title=axl, a transforming gene isolated from primary human myeloid leukemia cells, encodes a novel receptor tyrosine kinase|journal=Molecular and Cellular Biology|volume=11 |issue=10 |pages=5016–5031 |language=EN|doi=10.1128/mcb.11.10.5016-5031.1991|pmid=1656220 |pmc=361494 |s2cid=44190723 }}</ref>), and deciphering the dynamics of gene regulation on a genomic scale that modulates cancer biology.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fullwood|first1=Melissa J.|last2=Liu|first2=Mei Hui|last3=Pan|first3=You Fu|last4=Liu|first4=Jun|last5=Xu|first5=Han|last6=Mohamed|first6=Yusoff Bin|last7=Orlov|first7=Yuriy L.|last8=Velkov|first8=Stoyan|last9=Ho|first9=Andrea|last10=Mei|first10=Poh Huay|last11=Chew|first11=Elaine G. Y.|date=2009|title=An oestrogen-receptor-α-bound human chromatin interactome|journal=Nature|language=en|volume=462|issue=7269|pages=58–64|doi=10.1038/nature08497|issn=0028-0836|pmc=2774924|pmid=19890323|bibcode=2009Natur.462...58F }}</ref> His work has spanned basic to population sciences to translation to the clinic. He has authored over 320 scientific papers and reviews, and co-authored two books.
